Case: Password step is displayed without any notice when an existing email is entered at sign-up
Description:
• Pre-condition: An account already exists in SleekFlow with email address X (email/password login). User is on the sign-up identifier screen (step 1).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-005 · AC1
  • Note: This TC documents current Auth0 behavior (SU-03). Expected behavior will change once D1 is resolved per AC2.
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the sign-up identifier screen.
  2. Enter email address X (already registered) and accept consent.
  3. Click Continue.
  4. Observe whether any warning or notice about the existing account is shown.
  5. Observe which screen is displayed next.
Expected:
• No notice about an existing account is displayed on step 1.
  • User is silently moved to the password step (step 2).
  • The email field on step 2 shows email X in read-only state.
BDD: Given an email address already registered with SleekFlow is entered at sign-up, When the user submits step 1, Then the user advances silently to the password step with no duplicate-account notice

Case: Registration failure message is displayed when password is submitted for an email that already has an account
Description:
• Pre-condition: An account already exists in SleekFlow with email address X. User has reached the password step (step 2) using email X via sign-up.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-005 · AC1
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the sign-up flow with an already-registered email X.
  2. Arrive at the password step.
  3. Enter any valid complex password.
  4. Click Submit.
  5. Observe the resulting message or screen.
Expected:
• Auth0 displays an error message: "We couldn\u2019t complete your registration. Please try again or contact us for support." (note: right-single-quote U+2019 in "couldn\u2019t" is rendered correctly).
  • User is not logged in or registered.
  • User remains on or is returned to an error state page.
BDD: Given a user is on the password step using an already-registered email, When a valid password is submitted, Then Auth0 displays a registration failure message and no new account is created

Case: Defined behavior for existing email at sign-up is applied after D1 decision is made
Description:
• Pre-condition: D1 decision has been made by Product and Security. An account already exists with email X. User is on the sign-up identifier screen.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-005 · AC2
  • Note (BLOCKING TBD — D1): This TC cannot be executed until Product + Security decide between D1(a) no-enumeration + email notification or D1(b) on-screen message with sign-in link. TC is flagged Manual.
Test Steps:
1. Confirm D1 decision (a or b) has been implemented.
  2. Navigate to the sign-up identifier screen.
  3. Enter already-registered email X and accept consent.
  4. Click Continue.
  5. Observe the response shown to the user.
Expected:
• EXPECTED (D1a): User sees same screen as a new sign-up with no account-existence hint. Owner of email X receives an out-of-band email: "You already have an account — sign in or reset".
  • EXPECTED (D1b): An on-screen message indicates the account exists, with a sign-in link provided.
  • Either way: no new duplicate account is created.
BDD: Given D1 is implemented and an already-registered email is entered at sign-up, When the user submits step 1, Then the system responds per the D1 decision without creating a duplicate account

Case: Account owner receives an email notification when their email is used in a sign-up attempt under D1(a)
Description:
• Pre-condition: D1(a) has been chosen and implemented. An account exists with email X. A different user attempts to sign up using email X.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-005 · AC2
  • Note (BLOCKING TBD — D1): This TC applies only if D1(a) is chosen. Flagged Manual pending D1 resolution.
Test Steps:
1. Confirm D1(a) is implemented.
  2. Navigate to the sign-up identifier screen and enter email X.
  3. Complete step 1 (sign-up attempt).
  4. Check the inbox of email X for a notification email.
  5. Open the notification email and read its content.
Expected:
• An email notification is delivered to the inbox of email X within a reasonable time (e.g., under 5 minutes).
  • Email subject and body indicate the account already exists and provide options to sign in or reset password.
  • No account enumeration occurs on the sign-up screen (attacker learns nothing from the UI response).
BDD: Given D1(a) is implemented and email X already has an account, When a sign-up attempt is made with email X, Then the account owner receives an email notification to sign in or reset
